{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = 'data/sales.csv'
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Convert `revenue` from string with commas to float
data['revenue_numeric'] = data['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Identify QA orders (revenue == 999999.99)
qa_orders = data[data['revenue_numeric'] == 999999.99]

# Check if any QA orders are in the group of NEW customers reached by PAID SEARCH
filtered_qa = qa_orders[(qa_orders['channel'] == 'paid_search') & (qa_orders['customer_segment'] == 'new')]
print(f'Number of QA orders among NEW customers reached by PAID SEARCH: {len(filtered_qa)}')

# Since it's 2, the QA orders ARE in the filtered group
# This means they are affecting the conversion rate calculation
# We must remove them from the dataset before computing the conversion rate

# Create a clean dataset without QA orders
clean_data = data[data['revenue_numeric'] != 999999.99]

# Now filter for NEW customers reached by PAID SEARCH in clean data
filtered_clean = clean_data[(clean_data['channel'] == 'paid_search') & (clean_data['customer_segment'] == 'new')]

# Compute conversion rate in clean data
converted_count_clean = filtered_clean['converted'].sum()
total_count_clean = len(filtered_clean)
conversion_rate_clean = converted_count_clean / total_count_clean

# Print the final value
conversion_rate_clean"}
